attribution: Traditionally attributed to Shankara; authorship debated by scholars
period: Date uncertain; if not by Shankara, likely a later Advaita primer
summary: A short prose primer that defines the basic vocabulary of Vedanta in question-and-answer form.
whyRead: Tattva Bodha is often the first text taught in traditional Vedanta study, because it defines the terms every later work assumes: the three bodies, five sheaths, three states, the elements and the kinds of karma. It is compact and orderly.
questions: What are the kinds of karma?
What is needed to begin Vedanta study?

keyTeachings.title: The fourfold qualification
keyTeachings.text: It begins by listing the qualifications of a seeker: discernment, dispassion, the six virtues and longing for liberation.

keyTeachings.title: Three bodies, five sheaths, three states
keyTeachings.text: It distinguishes gross, subtle and causal bodies, maps them onto the five sheaths, and relates them to waking, dream and deep sleep.

keyTeachings.title: Creation from the elements
keyTeachings.text: It outlines how the subtle and gross elements give rise to the body, senses and world.

keyTeachings.title: Three kinds of karma
keyTeachings.text: It distinguishes accumulated (sanchita), current (agami) and already-operating (prarabdha) karma, and explains what knowledge does to each.

relatedTexts.note: Develops the same themes at greater length
